content: Universities now grapple with AI writing tools as they once did with ghostwriting. In 2023, Vanderbilt University apologized after using ChatGPT for a condolence email, revealing persistent discomfort: even disclosed assistance feels deceptive. Current campus policies permit AI for editing but prohibit submitting generated content as original. Rules can ensure compliance, but public expectation remains unchanged—readers want authentic expression from named authors.

title: 9块9充话费，为什么突然消失了？
content: China's telecom operators have stopped third-party platforms from selling low-cost recharge options and cheap data SIM cards. Previously, users could recharge phone credit in small amounts (10-20 yuan) via WeChat or Alipay, and buy discounted data plans through e-commerce platforms. These options are now restricted to official operator apps, with minimum recharges starting at 50 yuan. While operators cite security concerns and expired contracts as reasons, deeper factors include market saturation, declining traditional revenue, and strategic shifts toward AI and computing services. Users face higher costs and fewer flexible options, though official channels offer more security. Consumer demand for affordable, convenient services persists unmet.

title: 长鑫存储开始试产 HBM3E 内存 有望数周内大规模量产
content: ChangXin Memory Technologies has begun trial production of HBM3E memory, with mass production expected within weeks. The company is expanding DRAM capacity to 350,000 wafers per month by year-end to meet AI and high-performance computing demand. ChangXin builds cleanrooms in 12 months, enabling rapid scaling. HBM3E features 1,024-bit width, 9.2–12.4 Gbps per-pin speed, 1.2 TB/s bandwidth, and 24GB (8-layer) or 36GB (12-layer) capacities for AI accelerators and data centers.
